newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SUPREMA TO BUY VILNIAUS VINGIS LEFTOVERS.
newsitem.headline: SUPREMA TO BUY VILNIAUS VINGIS LEFTOVERS.

text.p: Lithuania's Suprema brokerage said on Thursday it planned to buy whatever is left of Vilniaus Vingis's share issue after the 30-day period of preemptive rights for current shareholders ends.
The securities commission last Friday registered 2.764 million new ordinary shares of the electronics components producer with a face value of five litas.

"Current shareholders have preemptive rights, starting yesterday, and after this period, we have an agreement (with Vilniaus Vingis) that we will take everything that will be left," Suprema head Aidas Galubickas told Reuters.
"I don't think that too many current shareholders will take shares," Galubickas said.
Suprema expects to pick up something "very near" 15 million litas worth of the new shares, Galubickas said.
"Say from 12 million litas to 16 million litas, probably, but generally I think it will be something like 15 million litas to 16 million litas," Galubickas said.
The share capital after the boost will stand at 45.62 million litas.
The issue price of the new shares is 5.8 litas, the company said Tuesday.
Vilniaus Vingis started the new share subscription on Wednesday with a 30-day priority right to current shareholders.
Vilniaus Vingis, an A-group company on the Vilnius bourse, said it was planning to use 75 percent of the funds raised by new issue to upgrade its production lines.
The company said it would use some 25 percent of the funds raised to boost its working capital.
